1. (Currently Amended) A lamp comprised of an at least substantially hollow columnar body, a plurality of light emitting diodes disposed on said columnar body, a plurality of fins disposed on said columnar body, a base member disposed at a first end of the columnar body and providing a means for electrical connection, and an electronics module disposed within the columnar body and in electrical communication with the base member, wherein the light emitting diodes are mounted on at least one exterior surface of the columnar body.

2. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein a second end of said columnar body is open and said columnar body is comprised of metal or metal alloy.

3. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 further including a light dispersing optic element overlapping at least one of said diodes.

4. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 3 wherein said optic element includes a phosphor material selected from the group consisting of yttrium aluminum garnet (YAG) phosphors and silicate phosphors.

5. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said diodes are mounted in a staggered configuration along said columnar body.

6. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 5 wherein said fins are arranged to alternate with the light emitting diodes.

7. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said columnar body comprises one of a tetragon, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon, decagon, hendecagon, or dodecagon in cross-section and wherein at least one light emitting diode is positioned to radiate through each face of said columnar body.

8. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 7 wherein at least one fin resides on each edge of said columnar body.

9. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 8 wherein a single diode resides on each face, and at least one diode is positioned adjacent to at least one fin.

10. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 9 wherein two diodes reside on each face, and at least one diode is positioned adjacent to one fin.

11. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said columnar body and said fins are comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 150 W/ mK.

12. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 9 including a single optic element disposed between each adjacent fin overlapping a diode.

13. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said base member comprises an Edison screw base or a wedge base made of a high thermal conductivity material.

14. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said electronics module comprises a printed circuit board including active and passive circuitry for converting AC to DC current.

15. (Currently Amended) The lamp of claim 3 wherein said optic element preferentially directs light in a radial direction relative to said columnar body.

16. (Currently Amended) A lamp comprising an elongated hollow polygonal body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 150 W/ mK, a fin extending radially from each corner of said body, a light emitting diode mounted to each side of said body, a screw or wedge base connector closing a first end of said body, a second end of said body being open, an electronics module disposed within said body in electrical communication with said connector and said light emitting diodes, said lamp having a general A19 outline adapted to accommodate heat dissipation.

17. (Currently Amended) A method of manufacturing a lamp comprising extruding an elongated hollow body, said body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 150 W/ mK, cutting said body to a predetermined length, attaching at least one light emitting diode to said body and providing electrical circuitry suitable for powering said light emitting diode while maintaining adequate thermal management.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein said material has a thermal conductivity greater than about 200 W/ mK.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein said body includes a plurality of integral radially extending fins arranged to enhance thermal dissipation.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 20 wherein said body has substantially vertical side walls for improved structural integrity.
